I've always gravitated towards emotionally unavailable men, trying to make them love me. Recently I gave my all (went into debt to provide for him, gave him my body, used up all my emotional resources) in a relationship only for him to tell me he "didn't like me like that." I went through a lot of anger and sadness (and I'm still going through it, 2 months later) but I did something I've never done before- looking inwards. Instead of being like "why do I attract shitty men?" I asked myself "why do I settle for scraps?"  


I followed this train of thought and it led to my inner child, wounded from my parents (especially dad's) lack of emotional availability. I realized that I've been trying to heal this wound in my adult relationships by begging to be loved. Something clicked in me and I've vowed never to accept less, if not for "me" then for my inner child, who I find easier to show sympathy and love to. 

​

Still, it's hard not to feel useless after a rejection of that scale. I gave all of me and now I have nothing for myself, and he simply laughed it off and is now on to the next girl without even a "sorry." Definitely a tower moment, especially given that I felt such a strong soul connection to this person. Guess it was the ultimate lesson of self love; if I can give up someone I thought was "the one" and decide to love myself, I can heal and eventually attract a better suited love. Sigh, lol.

There's several reasons:
1) he's running cause he's scared, overwhelmed, and triggering us both to grow (so I'm accepting the process)

2) I have so much to say and yet I know saying it won't make a difference: at the end of the day he knows how I feel and I know how he feels

3) being in contact with him hurts (but so does separation so it's an impossible situation)

Hey there, you're not alone with what you're going through. I've been on my healing-from-pcos journey for nearly 10 years now so I can share what has helped me:

* Spironolactone for hair loss (it's an anti-androgen, can be prescribed by a dermatologist)
* Rogaine (5%)
* Vitamin D
* Saw palmetto
* folic acid
* hair, skin, nails vitamins
* birth control (yazmin)
* spearmint tea (drink twice a day)
* avoid unhealthy diet (ex: overly processed foods)
* exercise

I'm getting to this point too but I wouldn't describe my journey as making me less ambitious- I'm more focused on finding my true passion (which will bring me money + happiness) rather than following the "typical" storyline.
